Plot the Pareto Frontier of Candidate Subgroups

Source: R/plot_pareto_frontier.R
plot_pareto_frontier.Rd

Produces a 2D scatter of candidate subgroups in (effect, N) space, with the Pareto frontier drawn as a step polyline and the selected subgroup highlighted. When ci_table is supplied (the return value of compute_frontier_cis), horizontal error bars for the split-derived 95\

Usage

plot_pareto_frontier(
  fs,
  ci_table = NULL,
  show_band = FALSE,
  effect_neighborhood = NULL,
  label_members = TRUE,
  point_size = 3,
  xlim = NULL,
  xlim_trim = NULL
)

Arguments

fs

A forestsearch result object.

ci_table

Optional data.table from compute_frontier_cis. When supplied, horizontal error bars depict the split-derived 95\ Default NULL (no error bars).

show_band

Logical. If TRUE and sg_focus is "hrMaxSG" or "hrMinSG", shade the effect-size neighborhood band on the right of the plot. Default FALSE.

effect_neighborhood

Numeric. Override of the band width; defaults to the value used in the original forestsearch call (or 0.10 if not recoverable).

label_members

Logical. If TRUE, label each frontier member with its short cut description. Default TRUE.

point_size

Numeric. Size of frontier-member points. Default 3.

xlim

Optional numeric vector of length 2 controlling the x-axis range, e.g.\ c(0.5, 3). By default the axis auto-expands to include split-CI bars when supplied, which can make individual points look crowded. Pass an explicit xlim (or use xlim_trim = TRUE) to zoom in.

xlim_trim

Logical or NULL. If TRUE (and xlim is NULL), the x-axis is trimmed to the range of frontier point estimates with a small padding, ignoring CI bars. If NULL (default), auto-decides: TRUE when the effect measure is on a ratio (log) scale ("OR", "RR", "IRR"), where wide split-CI tails on the natural scale routinely dwarf the point-estimate range and force the axis to span orders of magnitude; FALSE otherwise. Pass TRUE or FALSE explicitly to override the auto behavior.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The frontier polyline is drawn as a downward step from large-effect / small-N candidates to small-effect / large-N candidates. Points off the frontier (if any are present in the fs$grp.consistency$out_sg$result table beyond those on the frontier) are not currently plotted; this function only displays the frontier and its selected member.

For sg_focus = "hrMinSG", the selected subgroup may not lie on the Pareto frontier (the focus deliberately prefers small subgroups, which are typically N-dominated). In that case the selected marker appears off the polyline.

See also

pareto_frontier_table, compute_frontier_cis, frontier_member_flags.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
p <- plot_pareto_frontier(fs)
print(p)

# With split-derived 95% CIs:
ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(fs, n_splits = 1000)
p2 <- plot_pareto_frontier(fs, ci_table = ci_tab)
print(p2)
} # }
